questions.q: What problem does a branching strategy solve at team scale that it doesn't at the individual level?
options: It stops Git from allowing more than one branch to exist
Without a shared answer to where work starts and when it merges, nobody can predict where work lives or when it's safe to release
It makes commits run faster
It is required before any team can use GitHub at all
questions.explain: Branching itself is cheap for one person; the coordination problem only appears once multiple people need predictable, shared conventions.

questions.q: In Git Flow, what is the purpose of a release/* branch?
options: It stabilizes a specific release with bug fixes only, forked from develop, then merges into both main and develop
It replaces main permanently
It is used for every new feature instead of feature/*
It automatically deploys to production on creation
questions.explain: A release branch is cut from develop to stabilize a release candidate; once ready it merges into main (tagged) and back into develop.

questions.q: What makes a hotfix/* branch different from a feature/* branch in Git Flow?
options: A hotfix branch forks directly from main for an urgent production fix, rather than from develop like a feature branch
A hotfix branch never gets merged anywhere
There is no difference — they're the same thing
A hotfix branch can only be created by GitHub support
questions.explain: Hotfix branches skip the normal develop-based flow entirely, branching from main to address an urgent production issue immediately.

questions.q: How does trunk-based development keep merge conflicts manageable?
options: By disabling merge conflicts entirely in Git settings
By never allowing more than one developer to work at a time
By requiring every branch to be reviewed by five people
By keeping feature branches short-lived, so nobody is reconciling weeks of divergence
questions.explain: Because branches merge back within a day or two in trunk-based development, there's far less time for main and a branch to diverge.

questions.q: What problem do feature flags solve in a trunk-based workflow?
options: They let unfinished code merge into main and even reach production while staying switched off, decoupling merging from releasing
They prevent any code from ever being merged
They are a Git Flow concept, not used in trunk-based development
They automatically write commit messages
questions.explain: Feature flags let teams merge early without shipping an incomplete feature to real users, which is essential when main is always close to what's deployed.
